# iwe enhancements for structured note management

## Overview

Three changes to iwe (the Rust tool), plus a separate task-management wrapper. The iwe changes are general-purpose features useful to any knowledge graph; the wrapper adds project-specific workflow policy.

## Boundary principle

If someone using iwe for a photography knowledge base would find the feature useful, it goes in iwe. Metadata filtering, virtual directories — yes. Status transitions, gate enforcement — no. Those are opinions about workflow that belong in a wrapper.

---

## 1. Bare front matter support (iwe)

### Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: ` (literal, case-sensitive, space required after colon)
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line (strict `\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n` only — a line containing only whitespace is NOT a separator) are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives. No key whitelist needed — `title` as mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false`.

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (`crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` L26–33), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, call `wrap_bare_frontmatter(content)` which returns `Cow<str>`
- If content starts with `---`, return `Borrowed` (already fenced)
- If first line starts with `title: `, find first blank line, wrap the header block with `---` delimiters
- Otherwise return `Borrowed` (no front matter detected)
- Pass the wrapped content to `MarkdownEventsReader::read()`
- The downstream `MetadataBlock` handling already captures YAML into `Document.metadata` — no other reader changes needed

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled (`crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs`):
- In `block_events`, partition out the leading `GraphBlock::Frontmatter` block
- Do not push `MetadataBlock` events for it (pulldown_cmark_to_cmark always fences, can't bypass)
- In `write`, prepend the raw front matter text followed by a blank line before the rendered body
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand fenced front matter

### Config plumbing

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs`: add `#[serde(default)] pub bare_frontmatter: bool` to `MarkdownOptions`, default `false`
- Add v3→v4 config migration that bumps version (new fields use defaults)

### Tests (`crates/liwe/tests/bare_frontmatter_test.rs`, new file)

- `reader_detects_bare_title_block`: bare headers parsed as metadata
- `reader_skips_when_disabled`: same input with `bare_frontmatter=false` yields no metadata
- `reader_skips_when_no_title_first_line`: `date:` first line → no metadata
- `reader_does_not_misparse_prose`: prose starting line → no metadata
- `reader_still_handles_fenced`: `---` fenced input works when `bare_frontmatter=true`
- `writer_emits_bare_when_enabled`: round-trip preserves bare format
- `writer_emits_fenced_when_disabled`: round-trip produces fenced output
- `frontmatter_title_works_with_bare`: link text update from bare front matter title

### Dependencies

Config plumbing (Phase 0) must land first.

---

## 2. Metadata filtering on `find` (iwe)

### Problem

iwe already parses and stores front matter YAML per document (`Graph.metadata: HashMap<Key, String>`). But `find` can't filter on it. The only metadata access is `extract_frontmatter_title` for a single configured key.

### Design

Add `--meta key=value` to `iwe find`. Multiple `--meta` flags combine with AND.

```bash
iwe find --meta status=ready              # tasks ready to start
iwe find --meta status=design             # tasks needing design
iwe find --meta camera=Leica              # photography notes
iwe find --meta status=active --roots     # combinable with existing flags
```

### Implementation

**`crates/liwe/src/graph.rs`**: add public accessor (after `get_key_title` at ~L215):
```rust
pub fn get_metadata(&self, key: &Key) -> Option<&str>
```

**`crates/liwe/src/find.rs`**:
- Add `metadata_filters: Vec<(String, String)>` to `FindOptions` (defaults to empty via `Default`)
- Add `metadata_matches(&self, key, filters)` method to `DocumentFinder`
- Filter in the candidate `filter_map`, after the `refs_from` check
- YAML value matching: strings compared directly, numbers/bools compared as strings, sequences use membership match (value present in list)

**`crates/iwe/src/main.rs`**: add `--meta` flag (repeatable) to `struct Find` with `parse_meta_filter` value parser that splits on `=`.

**`crates/iwes`**: leave `metadata_filters` empty in workspace symbol search (recompiles cleanly via `Default`).

### Tests (`crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs`, new file)

- `combines_filters_with_and`
- `non_matching_value_excluded`
- `note_without_metadata_excluded`

### Dependencies

Independent of Phase 1 (bare front matter), but Phase 0 (config) should land first.

---

## 3. Virtual directory nodes (iwe)

### Problem

Organizing notes into subdirectories (e.g., `tasks/`) requires a manual index note with inclusion links to each file. Adding or removing a note means updating the index. This is friction.

### Design

When `virtual_directories` is enabled, iwe auto-generates and maintains index files for directories containing `.md` files.

#### Naming convention

- `_tasks.md` — iwe-generated index for `tasks/` directory. The `_` prefix is the signal that this file is auto-managed. Visible from directory listing without reading file contents.
- `tasks.md` — user-maintained index. If this exists, iwe does not generate or read `_tasks.md`.

#### Key derivation

The `_` prefix is stripped during key derivation. Both `_tasks.md` and `tasks.md` produce key `tasks`. They cannot coexist: if `tasks.md` exists, `_tasks.md` is neither generated nor loaded.

#### Lifecycle

| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| `tasks/` has `.md` files, neither `tasks.md` nor `_tasks.md` exists | Generate `_tasks.md` |
| `tasks/` has `.md` files, `_tasks.md` exists, dir mtime > file mtime | Regenerate `_tasks.md` |
| `tasks/` has `.md` files, `_tasks.md` exists, file is current | Use as-is |
| `tasks.md` exists | Don't generate `_tasks.md`; if `_tasks.md` exists, delete it |
| User creates `tasks.md` | On next load, `_tasks.md` deleted, user file used |
| User deletes `tasks.md` | On next load, `_tasks.md` generated |

#### Generated content

```markdown
# tasks

[parse-error](tasks/parse-error)

[incremental-fts](tasks/incremental-fts)
```

Children listed as block-reference links (not transclusions), ordered alphabetically by key. Title is the raw directory basename.

Every directory that transitively contains `.md` files gets a generated index — not just leaf directories. This preserves filesystem hierarchy in the graph. A directory containing only subdirectories (no direct `.md` files) still gets an index whose children are the subdirectory index nodes.

#### Implementation

**`crates/liwe/src/fs.rs`** (`new_for_path`):
- After collecting `(key, content)` pairs, scan for directories containing `.md` files
- For each directory, check for user index (`dirname.md`) — if present, skip
- Check for generated index (`_dirname.md`) — if absent or stale, regenerate
- Strip `_` prefix when deriving key
- Gate on `virtual_directories` config (requires `new_for_path` to accept config or bool)

**`crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs`**: add `#[serde(default)] pub virtual_directories: bool` to `LibraryOptions`, default `false`.

### Config

```toml
[library]
virtual_directories = true
```

### Interaction with other features

- `iwe find` discovers generated index nodes like any other document (key `tasks`)
- `iwe tree` shows them with their children
- `iwe retrieve -k tasks -d 1` retrieves the index and its immediate children
- `--meta` filtering works on children (the generated index itself has no front matter)

### Tests (`crates/liwe/tests/virtual_directories_test.rs`, new file)

- `directory_with_notes_generates_index`
- `user_index_takes_precedence`
- `user_index_suppresses_generated`
- `generated_index_deleted_when_user_creates_own`
- `disabled_by_default`
- `children_alphabetical_order`
- `nested_directories_each_get_index`
- `underscore_stripped_from_key`

### Dependencies

Phase 0 (config). Phase 2 should land first so `--meta` tests can verify filtering on children of virtual nodes.

---

## 4. Task management wrapper (separate from iwe)

### What it is

A shell script named `iwe` that sits ahead of the real `iwe` on PATH. It intercepts task-specific commands and delegates everything else to the real iwe.

### What it adds

**`iwe update -k <key> --set <field>=<value>`** — field-level front matter mutation with policy enforcement:
- Read note via `iwe retrieve`
- Parse YAML, modify field
- Enforce transition rules (e.g., can't go from `design` to `done`)
- Check gates before allowing `done` transition
- Write back via real `iwe update`

### Phase 1 — Bare front matter support

#### 1a. Reader: pre-wrap bare headers with `---`

**File: `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`** (`MarkdownReader::document`, L26–33)

This is the cleanest injection point — it owns the `&str` content right
before it goes into `MarkdownEventsReader::read`. Add a helper:

```rust
fn wrap_bare_frontmatter(content: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> { ... }
```

Logic, gated on `markdown_options.bare_frontmatter`:

1. If `content` starts with `---` (optionally preceded by a UTF-8 BOM /
   leading whitespace? — see Open Question Q1) → return `Borrowed`.
2. Find first line. If it does not start with `title: ` (literal, including
   the space) → return `Borrowed`.
3. Find the index of the first blank line (`\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n`, or EOF).
4. Split into `header_block` and `rest`. Return
   `Owned(format!("---\n{header_block}\n---\n\n{rest}"))`.

Then `MarkdownReader::document` calls `reader.read(&wrapped)` instead of
`reader.read(content)`. The downstream pipeline already handles
`MetadataBlock` events (see `reader.rs` L356, L386 — the
`Tag::MetadataBlock(_)` arms toggle `metadata_block`, and the `Text` arm
captures the YAML into `self.metadata`). No other reader changes required.

#### 1b. Writer: emit bare headers when configured

**File: `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs`**

`MarkdownWriter` already holds `options: MarkdownOptions` (L13). The
frontmatter is emitted at L41–49 in `block_events` for
`GraphBlock::Frontmatter(content)`, currently always as a
`MetadataBlock(YamlStyle)` event pair.

Two viable approaches:

- **Approach A (preferred):** When `self.options.bare_frontmatter`, do not
  push the `MetadataBlock` events at all. Instead, prepend the bare header
  text directly to the output string in `MarkdownWriter::write` (L21–30):
  call `cmark_with_options` for non-frontmatter blocks, then prefix
  `format!("{}\n\n", content.trim_end())` from the (single) Frontmatter
  block. Reason: pulldown_cmark_to_cmark always wraps `MetadataBlock` in
  `---`, so we cannot get bare output through it. Implementation: in
  `blocks_events`, partition out the leading `Frontmatter` block; in
  `write`, when bare mode and a leading frontmatter exists, write it raw
  first, then the rendered remainder.

- **Approach B:** Post-process the rendered string to strip the leading
  `---\n…\n---` and replace with bare lines. Brittle; reject.

Take Approach A.

#### 1c. Wiring callers

`MarkdownReader::document` already takes `markdown_options: &MarkdownOptions`
(`crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` L26), and `Graph::from_state` /
`Graph::from_markdown` (`graph.rs` L272, L347) thread it through. No
caller-site changes needed for the reader.

For the writer: instances are constructed in
`crates/liwe/src/model/tree.rs` and `crates/liwe/src/model/document.rs`
(grep for `MarkdownWriter::new`). They already receive `MarkdownOptions`
along the same path; just verify each site passes the loaded options rather
than `MarkdownOptions::default()`. (Spot-check needed during

  ```rust
  fn metadata_matches(&self, key: &Key, filters: &[(String, String)]) -> bool {
      let raw = match self.graph.get_metadata(key) { Some(s) => s, None => return false };
      let val: serde_yaml::Value = match serde_yaml::from_str(raw) { Ok(v) => v, _ => return false };
      filters.iter().all(|(k, v)| {
          val.get(k.as_str())
              .and_then(|node| match node {
                  serde_yaml::Value::String(s) => Some(s.as_str() == v),
                  serde_yaml::Value::Bool(b)   => Some(b.to_string() == *v),
                  serde_yaml::Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string() == *v),
                  serde_yaml::Value::Sequence(items) => Some(items.iter().any(|i| {
                      i.as_str().map(|s| s == v).unwrap_or(false)
                  })),
                  _ => Some(false),
              })
              .unwrap_or(false)
      })
  }
  ```
  (Sequence handling = "value present in list" — see Open Question Q3.)

**File: `crates/liwe/src/graph.rs`**

- If so, all lines up to the first blank line (strict `\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n` only — a line containing only whitespace is NOT a separator) are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

## 3. Virtual directory nodes (iwe)

### Problem

Organizing notes into subdirectories (e.g., `tasks/`) requires a manual index note with inclusion links to each file. Adding or removing a note means updating the index. This is friction.

### Design

When `virtual_directories` is enabled, iwe auto-generates and maintains index files for directories containing `.md` files.

#### Naming convention

- `_tasks.md` — iwe-generated index for `tasks/` directory. The `_` prefix is the signal that this file is auto-managed. Visible from directory listing without reading file contents.
- `tasks.md` — user-maintained index. If this exists, iwe does not generate or read `_tasks.md`.

#### Key derivation

The `_` prefix is stripped during key derivation. Both `_tasks.md` and `tasks.md` produce key `tasks`. They cannot coexist: if `tasks.md` exists, `_tasks.md` is neither generated nor loaded.

#### Lifecycle

| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| `tasks/` has `.md` files, neither `tasks.md` nor `_tasks.md` exists | Generate `_tasks.md` |
| `tasks/` has `.md` files, `_tasks.md` exists, dir mtime > file mtime | Regenerate `_tasks.md` |
| `tasks/` has `.md` files, `_tasks.md` exists, file is current | Use as-is |
| `tasks.md` exists | Don't generate `_tasks.md`; if `_tasks.md` exists, delete it |
| User creates `tasks.md` | On next load, `_tasks.md` deleted, user file used |
| User deletes `tasks.md` | On next load, `_tasks.md` generated |

#### Generated content

```markdown
# tasks

[parse-error](tasks/parse-error)

[incremental-fts](tasks/incremental-fts)
```

Children listed as block-reference links (not transclusions), ordered alphabetically by key. Title is the raw directory basename.

Every directory that transitively contains `.md` files gets a generated index — not just leaf directories. This preserves filesystem hierarchy in the graph. A directory containing only subdirectories (no direct `.md` files) still gets an index whose children are the subdirectory index nodes.

#### Implementation

**`crates/liwe/src/fs.rs`** (`new_for_path`):
- After collecting `(key, content)` pairs, scan for directories containing `.md` files
- For each directory, check for user index (`dirname.md`) — if present, skip
- Check for generated index (`_dirname.md`) — if absent or stale, regenerate
- Strip `_` prefix when deriving key
- Gate on `virtual_directories` config (requires `new_for_path` to accept config or bool)

**`crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs`**: add `#[serde(default)] pub virtual_directories: bool` to `LibraryOptions`, default `false`.

### Config

```toml
[library]
virtual_directories = true
```

### Interaction with other features

- `iwe find` discovers generated index nodes like any other document (key `tasks`)
- `iwe tree` shows them with their children
- `iwe retrieve -k tasks -d 1` retrieves the index and its immediate children
- `--meta` filtering works on children (the generated index itself has no front matter)

#### 1a. Reader: pre-wrap bare headers with `---`

**File: `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`** (`MarkdownReader::document`, L26–33)

This is the cleanest injection point — it owns the `&str` content right
before it goes into `MarkdownEventsReader::read`. Add a helper:

```rust
fn wrap_bare_frontmatter(content: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> { ... }
```

Logic, gated on `markdown_options.bare_frontmatter`:

1. If `content` starts with `---` (optionally preceded by a UTF-8 BOM /
   leading whitespace? — see Open Question Q1) → return `Borrowed`.
2. Find first line. If it does not start with `title: ` (literal, including
   the space) → return `Borrowed`.
3. Find the index of the first blank line (`\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n`, or EOF).
4. Split into `header_block` and `rest`. Return
   `Owned(format!("---\n{header_block}\n---\n\n{rest}"))`.

Then `MarkdownReader::document` calls `reader.read(&wrapped)` instead of
`reader.read(content)`. The downstream pipeline already handles
`MetadataBlock` events (see `reader.rs` L356, L386 — the
`Tag::MetadataBlock(_)` arms toggle `metadata_block`, and the `Text` arm
captures the YAML into `self.metadata`). No other reader changes required.

#### 1b. Writer: emit bare headers when configured

**File: `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs`**

frontmatter is emitted at L41–49 in `block_events` for

- **Approach A (preferred):** When `self.options.bare_frontmatter`, do not
  push the `MetadataBlock` events at all. Instead, prepend the bare header
  text directly to the output string in `MarkdownWriter::write` (L21–30):

  `format!("{}\n\n", content.trim_end())` from the (single) Frontmatter

  `---`, so we cannot get bare output through it. Implementation: in
  `blocks_events`, partition out the leading `Frontmatter` block; in
  `write`, when bare mode and a leading frontmatter exists, write it raw
  first, then the rendered remainder.

I found the likely culprit: the bare-frontmatter wrapper is “cleaning” the header by dropping every line that starts with a space before handing it to the normal fenced-YAML parser. That destroys indented YAML sequence items:

```yaml
title: A
depends:
  - foo
```

becomes:

```yaml
title: A
depends:
```

So `--meta depends=foo` has nothing to match. Fenced YAML bypasses this wrapper, which explains the reported asymmetry. I’ll add a regression test for bare frontmatter + sequence metadata, remove that destructive filtering, then run the tests.

## Diagnosis

`iwe find --meta depends=foo` depends on YAML sequence membership matching. The failure mode is caused when bare frontmatter wrapping destroys indented YAML lines before parsing, e.g.:

```yaml
title: Task A
depends:
  - foo
```

If those indented `- foo` lines are stripped, the metadata becomes effectively:

```yaml
title: Task A
depends:
```

so `depends=foo` cannot match. Fenced YAML does not go through the bare-frontmatter wrapper, which explains why fenced frontmatter worked.

One important note: `.indexnudge-rust.db` showed the destructive indentation-stripping code, but the actual source file on disk already preserved header indentation. I verified the real CLI path with a temp workspace and added regressions to lock the behavior down.

## Changes made

Added regression coverage in:

- `crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs`
  - `bare_frontmatter_yaml_sequence_matches`
  - Verifies library-level `DocumentFinder` matches `--meta depends=foo` against bare frontmatter YAML sequences.

- `crates/iwe/tests/find_test.rs`
  - `test_find_meta_matches_bare_frontmatter_yaml_sequence`
  - Verifies the actual CLI/config path with `bare_frontmatter = true`.

No production source diff was needed because the working source already preserves indented YAML sequence lines in `wrap_bare_frontmatter`.

## Verification

Ran:

```bash
cargo test -p liwe bare_frontmatter_yaml_sequence_matches --test find_metadata_test
cargo test -p iwe test_find_meta_matches_bare_frontmatter_yaml_sequence --test find_test
cargo test
```

All passed.

```text
crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs
```

